prompt: Which email marketing tool is easiest to use for a beginner?

trials.response:
For a complete beginner, **MailerLite is probably the easiest overall**. Its interface is deliberately simple, the drag-and-drop editor is straightforward, subscriber management isn’t overly complex, and its own onboarding is built around getting a first campaign running quickly. MailerLite

I’d roughly frame the main options like this:

| Tool | Beginner friendliness | Best fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Small businesses, simple newsletters, landing pages, basic automation |
| **Kit** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ | Creators, newsletters, digital products |
| **Brevo** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Businesses wanting email + transactional email/CRM features |
| **Mailchimp** | ⭐⭐⭐½ | General small-business marketing, especially if you already use its ecosystem |

**Kit** is also very beginner-friendly, particularly if your business is basically “build an audience → send newsletters → sell something.” It has dedicated beginner training and a relatively simple Broadcast/Sequence workflow. Kit Help Center+1

**Brevo** has an easy visual campaign workflow and drag-and-drop editor, but there are more CRM/transactional-marketing features around it, so it can feel slightly busier when you're new. Brevo Help+1

**Mailchimp** is still beginner-accessible and has extensive beginner guidance, but it has accumulated a lot of marketing functionality over the years, so I wouldn't choose it purely because you want the simplest interface. Mailchimp

So if you asked me, **“I’ve never done email marketing before; what should I open and start using today?” → MailerLite.** If you're specifically building a creator/newsletter business, I'd put **Kit** right beside it.

For a complete beginner, **MailerLite is probably the easiest email marketing tool to start with right now**. Its interface is relatively uncluttered, the campaign builder is drag-and-drop, and an independent 2026 review from EmailTooltester specifically rated it highly for ease of use and described its workflow as straightforward for beginners. **\[EmailTooltester.com\]**

### Why I'd start with MailerLite

You can create campaigns with drag-and-drop editors, build signup forms and landing pages, and set up visual automations without dealing with a particularly complex interface. Its current free plan includes **up to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails/month**, plus three automations, signup forms, and a landing page. Paid plans currently start around **$12/month**. MailerLite+1

**Brevo** would be my second choice. Its campaign creation process is also quite visual and beginner-friendly, and its editor doesn't require coding. Brevo Help+1

**Mailchimp** is still reasonably beginner-friendly—Mailchimp says a first campaign can be launched in under 15 minutes—but the platform has grown into a much larger marketing suite, so there are simply more menus/features to learn. Mailchimp+1

So if you told me:

> **"I've never done email marketing before. Just give me one tool."**

I'd choose **MailerLite**.

One caveat: MailerLite's account/website approval process can be stricter than some competitors, which is worth knowing if you're creating a brand-new business without an established website. **\[EmailTooltester.com\]**
